clue.text: Nark not running after money

indicators.note: after places the word for not running behind the word for money

parts.note: brass is old British slang for money
a machine that is not running is switched off

explanation.surface: A police informer stops working once the cash arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nark' looks like the British slang noun for a police informer; here it is the slang verb meaning to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: To nark is British slang for to annoy or irritate, the same sense as the colloquial phrase.

clue.text: Bidding elite guards come again?

indicators.note: guards means the word for elite surrounds the query

parts.note: the elite are the best
a request to repeat yourself, like eh?

explanation.surface: Elite bodyguards are being asked to return.
explanation.definitionFit: To act at someone's command or request is to act at their bidding.

clue.text: Soldier perhaps descending on border town in Ireland

indicators.note: in a down clue the soldier comes down on top of the border, so it is written first

parts.note: a soldier ant is one kind of ant, hence the 'perhaps'
a border or edge is a rim

explanation.surface: A soldier parachutes into a frontier town in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This town north-west of Belfast gives its name to a county of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Not forced to support player often dealing with high bar

indicators.note: in a down clue, to support means coming below the other pieces

parts.note: bridge write-ups name the players by compass points, and South is taken as the usual dealer
a high point is a peak
something done without force or strain is easy

explanation.surface: A relaxed card player deals with a tall bar.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge columns the players are North, South, East and West; the blog queries whether South really deals most. Speakeasies were illicit bars in US Prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: During US Prohibition an illegal drinking den selling liquor was given this name.

clue.text: Volunteers recruited by motor-racing appeal do very well

indicators.note: recruited by means the volunteers are taken in among the other letters

parts.note: F1, Formula One, with the 1 written as the Roman I
SA is short for sex appeal
the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve
to do someone is to swindle, or fiddle

explanation.surface: A motor-racing appeal recruits volunteers and does very well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recruited by' puts the volunteers inside the racing and appeal letters. The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's volunteer reserve; 'do' is the verb meaning cheat, not a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone in excellent health, in perfect shape.

clue.text: Fruit pop from America's sound when it repeats

indicators.note: when it repeats says the spoken word is given twice over
the word is said the way an American would pronounce it, which changes its spelling

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, so PA

explanation.surface: An American dad's way of speaking sounds odd when said twice.
explanation.walkthrough: In an American accent PA comes out as PAW; saying it twice gives the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya, and a North American tree of the custard-apple family, bear a soft edible fruit by this name.

clue.text: May I, after I've gone out?

definitions.text: May I, after I've gone out?

parts.words: May I, after I've gone out?
parts.note: the speaker is the month before May: the first of May arrives once this month has run out

explanation.surface: A polite request to follow once someone has left.
explanation.definitionFit: The month preceding May ends just before the first day of May begins.

clue.text: Before touring in two different guises, marks one's debut

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the two words for before go round the other letters

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
ere is an old word for before
M is an abbreviation for marks, as in the old German currency
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Before going on tour in two disguises, an actor marks the start of a career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in two different guises' says 'Before' supplies two different words, and 'touring' sends them round the letters for marks and one; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A first public performance of a play or film is its opening night.

clue.text: Little daughter cramming knows when sats are

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

indicators.note: cramming means the word for knows is stuffed with the daughter

parts.note: ken is Scots for know, so kens means knows

explanation.surface: A young girl crams to learn when her school tests are.
explanation.walkthrough: SATs are British school exams, but here 'sats' is short for Saturdays.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturdays fall in the two days closing each seven-day stretch.

clue.text: Over time affected by what brave chap is up to now

parts.note: to be hit by something is to be affected by it

indicators.note: Over says the word for a brave chap lies over, covering, the letter for time

parts.note: a brave chap is a hero

explanation.surface: Over the years a man has been changed by the courage of a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' says the brave chap covers the time letter; 'by' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal adverb meaning until this point in time, previously.

clue.text: Walk in the park to get the fresh air?

definitions.meaning: an informal phrase for a very easy task
a light wind brings a draught of fresh air

explanation.surface: A stroll in a park for some fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a very easy task is a cinch, and a gentle wind carrying fresh air is the literal sense.

clue.text: I entered in my pin in my confusion, being very precise

indicators.note: entered says the letter I goes into the mixed letters
in confusion means the letters of in my pin in my are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone muddles typing in a PIN while being terribly fussy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' rearranges IN MY PIN IN MY and 'entered' puts I among them. The rare phrase appears in Gilbert and Sullivan's Patience.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone affectedly dainty, fussy and prim.

clue.text: Oil well to render this?

parts.note: a leaking oil well spreads a film of oil across water, and the word for that film also means smoothly and well done

explanation.surface: Would an oil well produce this, done well?
explanation.definitionFit: A leaking well spreads a film of oil across water, which has this name; the adjective also means smooth and polished.

clue.text: Drawing quiet breath

parts.note: quiet and motionless means still
breath stands for being alive, as in the breath of life

explanation.surface: Someone drawing a quiet breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' pairs with 'breath' to suggest inhaling; it is the definition, a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The genre of painting or sketching inanimate objects such as fruit and vases is one kind of drawing.

clue.text: During interval, bishop and cardinal getting plastered, beamed

indicators.note: During says bishop sits inside the word for interval

parts.note: the break between the halves of a game is half-time
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
cardinals wear scarlet, so the colour stands for them

explanation.surface: At the match break two churchmen get drunk and grin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' and 'beamed' look like drunk, smiling clergy; together they describe a building with a timber frame infilled with plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Tudor-style buildings show exposed wooden beams with plaster filling the gaps between them.

clue.text: Possibly digs plot — something not to be missed!

parts.note: a flower bed is a garden plot
in cricket a sitter is an easy catch no fielder should drop

explanation.surface: A garden bed is a feature you really must see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' looks like a gardening verb beside 'plot', but it is British slang for rented lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is slang for lodgings, and a single rented room for living and sleeping is one kind.

clue.text: Thursday's so long coming round, while I think of it!

indicators.note: coming round means the farewell goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: so long is a farewell, the same as bye-bye
TH is the abbreviation for Thursday

explanation.surface: Thursday seems so long in coming, I suddenly remember.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces an aside, meaning incidentally, said when something springs to mind.

clue.text: Extra dependency on carbon emission

indicators.note: emission means the carbon is given off, removed from the word

parts.note: a dependency on a drug is an addiction
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Society's growing reliance on carbon emissions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something added as an extra is a supplement, an add-on.

clue.text: Tiresome gas bill I agree to send back repeatedly

indicators.note: send back means the pair of words is read backwards, and repeatedly asks for that turned pair three times over

parts.note: AD is short for advertisement, a bill or poster, and AY is a form of aye, meaning yes
AD is short for advertisement, a bill or poster, and AY is a form of aye, meaning yes
AD is short for advertisement, a bill or poster, and AY is a form of aye, meaning yes

explanation.surface: Someone keeps returning an irritating gas bill they had approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' is chatter, not fuel. 'send back repeatedly' turns the bill-and-agreement pair round, three times in all.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal, dismissive way of skipping dull, predictable talk, which is tedious chatter.

clue.text: Boat trips leave for island

indicators.note: trips suggests stumbling, so the letters of boat fall into a new order

parts.note: to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Boat trips depart for an island.
explanation.definitionFit: This Caribbean island forms a nation with its larger neighbour Trinidad.

clue.text: One ate oysters with chips

parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's poem a tusked sea creature and a carpenter eat the oysters; chips is old slang for a carpenter

explanation.surface: Someone dined on oysters with a side of fries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' suggests fried potatoes, but it is old slang for a carpenter: the clue recalls Carroll's poem in Through the Looking-Glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tusked Arctic sea mammal is the oyster-eater in Carroll's poem.

clue.text: Masses having initially to vote in round one twice

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word having
in places the word for voting among the repeated pair
twice says the round-and-one pair appears two times

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
one as a Roman numeral is I
to poll is to vote

explanation.surface: The public first get to vote in a round, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the vote between the two round-and-one pairs, after the first letter of 'having'.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek for 'the many', the phrase is used in English for ordinary people, the common herd.

clue.text: Love and marriage not for everyone: it can bring tears

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: not says the letter for everyone is dropped from the word for marriage

parts.note: a marriage is a union
U is the British film certificate for universal, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: Love and marriage don't suit everyone and can end in tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping this bulb vegetable releases a compound that makes eyes water.

clue.text: Backward hospital omitting to house place for GP

indicators.note: Backward says the hidden letters are read backwards
to house means the clue words hold the letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hospital goes backwards by failing to find room for a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft folded 'to house' into the definition, but it signals the letters held in 'hospital omitting'; the definition is 'place for GP'. ALOMI read backwards gives the Italian circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian town's racing circuit has staged Formula One Grands Prix, so it is a venue for one.

clue.text: Old officer producing book with a story-teller's confession

parts.note: a teller of tall stories might admit 'I lie'

explanation.surface: An elderly officer writes a book containing a fibber's admission.
explanation.walkthrough: A story-teller here is a liar. A BAILIE was a Scottish town magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland this was a municipal magistrate or alderman, a historical civic office-holder.

clue.text: Fired from one high-flying position, heading for another

definitions.text: Fired from one high-flying position, heading for another

parts.words: Fired from one high-flying position, heading for another
parts.note: a missile launched from one aircraft at another travels between two positions high in the sky; the surface suggests a sacked executive moving to a new top job

explanation.surface: A sacked executive moves from one top job straight to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes weapons launched by one aircraft against another in flight.

clue.text: Online version that's current

indicators.note: a version of a word is a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: An internet edition of the news that is up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: This warm Pacific Ocean current recurs every few years and disrupts weather worldwide.

clue.text: People caught by returning agent stifling scream

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: stifling says the word for agent wraps round and smothers the scream
returning means the word for agent is read backwards

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
something hilarious is a scream, or a riot

explanation.surface: Someone is caught when a turncoat agent muffles a scream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives YPS and 'stifling' puts RIOT inside it; 'by' links C to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of the Mediterranean island republic are its people.
